You are welcome to reuse material from this site. What you can do depends on

## Written content: CC BY 4.0

Guides, blog posts, slides, courses, the glossary and other text, with their
figures, are licensed under
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

You can copy, share and adapt them for any purpose, including commercial use,
as long as you credit the author, link to the source and say if you made
changes. For example:

> "Page title" by Tom Goodale, curiousstatistician.com, licensed under CC BY 4.0.

## Code examples and example datasets: CC0

Code examples shown in pages, the example datasets and the scripts that create
them are dedicated to the public domain under
[CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Use them however
you like, in your own analyses, teaching or software, with no need to credit
anyone.

## Apps and build scripts: MIT

The interactive apps, their code modules and the scripts that build this site
are released under the
[MIT licence](https://github.com/tgoodale/curiousstatistician/blob/main/LICENSE).
You can reuse and adapt the code if you keep the copyright and licence notice.

## Books
